words.en: a short, witty saying or poem
words.mnemonic: Epi + gram (likhna): chhoti, chatpati likhi baat.
words.example: "Brevity is the soul of wit" is a famous epigram.

words.en: a concluding section at the end of a book or play
words.mnemonic: Epi + logue: aakhri baat; opposite of prologue.
words.example: The epilogue tells us what happened to the characters later.

words.en: an event or part of a series
words.mnemonic: TV serial ke episodes = kadiyaan.
words.example: I watched three episodes of the show last night.

words.en: words written on a tombstone in memory of the dead
words.mnemonic: Epi + taph (kabr): kabr par likha lekh.
words.example: The epitaph read: 'Here lies a brave soldier.'

words.en: calmness and composure, especially in difficulty
words.mnemonic: Equa(l) + nimity (mann): dukh-sukh mein mann barabar.
words.example: She accepted the defeat with equanimity.

words.en: the gradual wearing away of soil or rock by wind or water
words.mnemonic: Erosion ~ erase: dheere-dheere mitna.
words.example: Trees help prevent soil erosion.

words.en: wrong; incorrect
words.mnemonic: Error + ous = galti wala.
words.example: The report was based on erroneous data.

words.en: to increase rapidly or become more intense
words.mnemonic: Escalator ki tarah upar chadhna.
words.example: The dispute escalated into a war.

words.en: to accompany someone for protection or guidance
words.mnemonic: Police escort = suraksha ke liye saath chalna.
words.example: Two guards escorted the minister to his car.

words.en: to roughly calculate or judge
words.mnemonic: Esti-MATE: dost se andaaza lagwana.
words.example: They estimated the cost at ten lakh rupees.

words.en: the wide mouth of a river where it meets the sea
words.mnemonic: Estuary ~ 'est' = end of river at sea.
words.example: The Narmada forms an estuary, not a delta.

words.en: lasting forever
words.mnemonic: E-TERNAL ~ 'internal' aatma - jo kabhi na mare.
words.example: They promised eternal friendship.

words.en: the study of the origin and history of words
words.mnemonic: Ety(mon) + logy: shabd ki janam-kundli.
words.example: The etymology of 'pyjama' goes back to Persian.

words.en: a feeling of intense happiness and excitement
words.mnemonic: Eu (achha) + phoria: khushi ka nasha.
words.example: There was euphoria in the country after the World Cup win.

words.en: the act of judging the value or quality of something
words.mnemonic: E-VALUE-ation: value nikalna.
words.example: The evaluation of answer sheets is in progress.

words.en: clearly seen or understood; obvious
words.mnemonic: Evident ~ evidence: saboot saamne - saaf.
words.example: It was evident that he was lying.

words.en: gradual development over time
words.mnemonic: Evolve = dheere dheere badalna; Darwin's theory.
words.example: Darwin explained the evolution of species.

words.en: to develop gradually
words.mnemonic: E-VOLVE ~ revolve: ghoom-ghoom kar dheere badalna.
words.example: The small shop evolved into a big company.

words.en: to make a problem or situation worse
words.mnemonic: Ex-ACERB ~ 'acid' daal diya - aur bura kar diya.
words.example: His rude reply only exacerbated the situation.

words.en: demanding great effort, care or skill
words.mnemonic: Exact + ing: sab kuch bilkul exact chahiye.
words.example: He is an exacting teacher who accepts no errors.

words.en: something that does not follow a general rule
words.mnemonic: Except = chhodkar; niyam se bahar.
words.example: Every rule has some exceptions.

words.en: an amount more than necessary
words.mnemonic: Ex + cess: hadd se zyada.
words.example: Eating sugar in excess is harmful.

words.en: to leave out or keep out
words.hi: बाहर रखना, अलग करना, छोड़ देना
words.mnemonic: Ex (bahar) + clude (band): bahar rakhna.
words.example: The price is Rs 500, excluding taxes.

words.en: in an extremely painful or intense way
words.mnemonic: Ex-CRUCI ~ crucify (soolee): soolee jaisa dard.
words.example: The wait was excruciatingly long.

words.en: to carry out a plan or order; to put to death legally
words.mnemonic: Executive = kaam karne wala; execute = kaam poora karna.
words.example: The plan was executed perfectly.

words.en: serving as a perfect example; excellent
words.mnemonic: Example + ary: misaal ban jaye aisa.
words.example: He was praised for his exemplary conduct.

words.en: freedom from a duty, tax or rule
words.mnemonic: Exempt = chhoot; tax exemption.
words.example: Senior citizens get exemptions on income tax.

words.en: physical or mental effort
words.mnemonic: Exert = zor lagana.
words.example: He was breathless after the exertion of climbing.

words.en: extremely tired; completely used up
words.mnemonic: Exhaust fan sab hawa bahar - taakat khatam.
words.example: After the long walk, we were exhausted.

words.en: to show publicly; to display
words.mnemonic: Exhibition = pradarshani.
words.example: The museum exhibits ancient coins.

words.en: a follower of existentialism, the philosophy stressing individual freedom and choice
words.mnemonic: Exist + ential: 'main kyon exist karta hoon?' sochne wala.
words.example: Sartre was a famous existentialist.

words.en: to declare someone free from blame
words.mnemonic: Ex + onus (bojh): aarop ka bojh hata dena.
words.example: The court exonerated him of all charges.

words.en: unreasonably high (of price or amount)
words.mnemonic: Ex + orbit: keemat orbit se bahar chali gayi.
words.example: The hotel charged exorbitant rates.

words.en: a person who drives out evil spirits
words.mnemonic: Exorcist ~ 'X out' the ghost - bhoot bahar.
words.example: The villagers called an exorcist to the haunted house.

words.en: foreign and unusual; from a distant country
words.mnemonic: Ex (bahar) se aaya - videshi, anokha.
words.example: The zoo has many exotic birds.

words.en: a belief that something will happen; hope
words.mnemonic: Expect = ummeed karna.
words.example: The results exceeded our expectations.

words.en: doing what is convenient or useful rather than what is right
words.mnemonic: Expedient ~ 'apna kaam nikalna' - sahi-galat nahi, fayda dekhna.
words.example: He acted out of political expediency.

words.en: to force someone to leave; to throw out
words.mnemonic: Ex + pel (dhakelna): bahar dhakel dena.
words.example: He was expelled from school for cheating.

words.en: the act of making amends for wrongdoing
words.mnemonic: Ex-PIATION ~ 'pious': paap dhone ke liye punya.
words.example: He fasted in expiation of his sins.

words.en: stated clearly and in detail
words.mnemonic: Ex + plicit: sab kuch khol kar bataya.
words.example: She gave explicit instructions to the staff.

words.en: a person who supports or is skilled in something; a power in maths
words.mnemonic: Expo(se) karne wala - kisi vichar ko aage rakhne wala.
words.example: Gandhi was a great exponent of non-violence.

words.en: extremely beautiful and delicate
words.mnemonic: Ex-QUISITE ~ 'ek-dum quality': bahut nafees, baareek kaarigari.
words.example: The temple has exquisite carvings.

words.en: to speak or perform without preparation
words.mnemonic: Ex + tempore (samay): samay par hi bol dena - extempore speech.
words.example: The speaker forgot his notes and had to extemporise.

words.en: to put out a fire or light; to end
words.mnemonic: Fire extinguisher - aag bujhane wala.
words.example: Firemen extinguished the blaze within an hour.

words.en: much too high in price; excessive
words.mnemonic: Extortion = jabran vasooli; keemat loot jaisi.
words.example: They charge extortionate fees.

words.en: to take or pull out
words.mnemonic: Ex + tract (kheenchna): bahar kheenchna.
words.example: The dentist extracted his tooth.

words.en: very unusual or remarkable
words.mnemonic: Extra + ordinary: saadharan se bahut upar.
words.example: She has an extraordinary talent for music.

words.en: spending too much money; excessive
words.mnemonic: Extra + vagant ~ 'extra' kharch karne wala.
words.example: He leads an extravagant lifestyle.

words.en: a person holding extreme political or religious views
words.mnemonic: Extreme + ist: hadd se aage ki soch.
words.example: The police arrested two extremists.

words.en: an outgoing, socially confident person
words.mnemonic: Extro (bahar) + vert (mudna): bahar ki taraf - logon se milne wala.
words.example: As an extrovert, he loves parties.

words.en: the quality of being full of energy and joy
words.mnemonic: Ex-UBER-ance: josh 'uber' (upar) tak.
words.example: The children's exuberance filled the room.

words.en: to invent false information; to construct
words.mnemonic: Fabric bunna - jhoothi kahaani bun dena.
words.example: He fabricated a story to avoid punishment.

words.en: treating serious matters with inappropriate humour
words.mnemonic: Face-tious: gambhir baat par 'face' banakar mazaak.
words.example: Stop being facetious; this is serious.

words.en: too simple; superficial; achieved easily
words.mnemonic: Facile ~ 'facility' se aasaan, par gehraai nahi.
words.example: He gave a facile answer to a complex question.

words.en: to make an action or process easier
words.mnemonic: Facility dena = kaam aasaan karna.
words.example: The new bridge will facilitate trade.

words.en: artificially created; not genuine
words.mnemonic: Facti-TIOUS ~ factory-made: nakli (not 'fictitious' = kaalpanik).
words.example: The crisis was factitious, created to raise prices.

words.en: based on facts
words.mnemonic: Fact + ual: tathyon par aadharit.
words.example: The report is purely factual.

words.en: loyal and constant; true to facts or the original
words.mnemonic: Faith + ful (full of faith): poora bharosa, wafadar. Spelling mein sirf ek 'l'.
words.example: The faithful dog waited for its master every evening.

words.en: based on a mistaken belief; misleading or false
words.mnemonic: Fallacious = 'fall' + 'lie': the argument falls because it rests on a lie.
words.example: His fallacious argument was quickly exposed by the judge.

words.en: a person with extreme, unreasonable enthusiasm for a cause or belief
words.mnemonic: Fan + attic: a fan so extreme he lives in the attic of his idol's house.
words.example: The religious fanatic refused to listen to any other opinion.

words.en: an absurd event or comedy based on ridiculous situations; a mockery
words.mnemonic: Farce sounds like 'face' of a joker, the whole show is a joke.
words.example: The trial was a farce because the verdict had been decided in advance.

words.en: extremely interesting and charming
words.mnemonic: Fascinating = 'fashion' show so attractive you can't look away.
words.example: She told us a fascinating story about her travels in Africa.

words.en: popular and in style at a particular time
words.mnemonic: Fashion + able = able to follow fashion, in trend.
words.example: Short hair became fashionable among young women that year.

words.en: very attentive to detail; hard to please; fussy
words.mnemonic: Fast-tedious: he makes every task tedious by checking every tiny detail.
words.example: He is fastidious about cleanliness and washes his hands constantly.

words.en: causing death or disaster
words.mnemonic: Fatal sounds like 'fate tal': fate decides your end.
words.example: The driver suffered fatal injuries in the crash.

words.en: a person who believes all events are predetermined and cannot be changed
words.mnemonic: Fatalist = believer in 'fate': jo kismat mein likha hai wahi hoga.
words.example: Being a fatalist, he made no effort to change his situation.

words.en: a defect or mistake; responsibility for something wrong
words.mnemonic: Fault = 'phaltu' mistake you are responsible for.
words.example: Despite all his faults, she loved him dearly.

words.en: possible and practical to do easily
words.mnemonic: Feasible = 'fees-able': if you can pay the fees, it's possible.
words.example: The engineers found that the plan was technically feasible.

words.en: lacking physical strength; weak
words.mnemonic: Feeble rhymes with 'fee-bill': paying big bills made him weak.
words.example: The old man raised a feeble hand to wave goodbye.

words.en: savagely fierce, cruel or violent
words.mnemonic: Ferocious = fierce + atrocious: a fierce, atrocious animal.
words.example: A ferocious tiger attacked the cattle near the village.

words.en: changing frequently, especially in loyalties or affections
words.mnemonic: Fickle sounds like 'phisle' (फिसले): mind keeps slipping from one thing to another.
words.example: Fame is fickle; today's star may be forgotten tomorrow.

words.en: not real or true; invented
words.mnemonic: Fictitious comes from fiction: made up like a story.
words.example: He gave a fictitious name to the police.

words.en: a place where fish are reared or caught; the industry of fishing
words.mnemonic: Fish + ery (place, like bakery): place for fish.
words.example: The coastal village depends on its fishery for income.

words.en: a long, narrow crack or opening in rock or earth
words.mnemonic: Fissure ~ 'fis-sure': surely a crack has formed.
words.example: Steam rose from a fissure in the volcanic rock.

words.en: a natural talent or aptitude for something
words.mnemonic: Flair sounds like 'flare': talent that shines like a flare.
words.example: She has a flair for languages and speaks five fluently.

words.en: a confident, showy and stylish manner
words.mnemonic: Flamboyance = flame + buoyant: bright as a flame, showing off.
words.example: The singer was known for the flamboyance of his costumes.

words.en: a person who praises others excessively and insincerely
words.mnemonic: Flatterer makes you feel 'flat-out' great with fake praise; chamcha.
words.example: The king was surrounded by flatterers who hid the truth from him.

words.en: without any defect or mistake; perfect
words.mnemonic: Flaw = defect; flaw-less = no defect.
words.example: She gave a flawless performance on stage.

words.en: to run away from danger
words.mnemonic: Flee rhymes with free: run away to be free.
words.example: Thousands of people had to flee their homes because of the flood.

words.en: the quality of bending easily or adapting to change
words.mnemonic: Flexible like a rubber band; flex-ibility = ability to flex.
words.example: The job offers flexibility in working hours.

words.en: able to bend easily; willing to change or adapt
words.mnemonic: Flex your muscles: flexible things can bend.
words.example: We need a flexible approach to solve this problem.

words.en: to throw forcefully or carelessly
words.mnemonic: Fling sounds like 'phenk-ing' (फेंकिंग).
words.example: In anger, he flung the book across the room.

words.en: not showing proper seriousness or respect
words.mnemonic: Flippant: he flips every serious topic into a joke.
words.example: The minister's flippant reply to the question angered the public.

words.en: to behave as if attracted to someone, but playfully, not seriously
words.mnemonic: Flirt ~ 'flutter': eyelashes fluttering playfully.
words.example: He liked to flirt with every girl at the party.

words.en: a group of sheep, goats or birds
words.mnemonic: Flock of sheep, flock of birds; 'lock' them together in one group.
words.example: A flock of sheep was grazing on the hillside.

words.en: to openly disregard a rule or law
words.mnemonic: Flout ~ 'flat out' rule todna: khule-aam niyam ki avhelna (flaunt = dikhava karna se confuse na karein).
words.example: Many drivers flout traffic rules when no police are around.

words.en: the peak period of development; the time of blooming
words.mnemonic: Flower blooms fully = flowering of art or culture.
words.example: The Gupta period saw the flowering of Indian art and literature.

words.en: the ability to speak or write easily and smoothly
words.mnemonic: Fluency flows like a fluid: words flow without stopping.
words.example: She speaks English with great fluency.

words.en: food for cattle and other livestock
words.mnemonic: Fodder sounds like 'food-er' for animals.
words.example: The farmers stored fodder for their cattle before winter.

words.en: a secure position or basis; a firm placing of the feet
words.mnemonic: Footing = where your foot stands firmly.
words.example: The company is now on a sound financial footing.

words.en: offensive to the senses; dirty; unfair or against the rules
words.mnemonic: Foul ball in cricket is unfair; foul smell is dirty.
words.example: A foul smell came from the blocked drain.

words.en: an entrance hall or lobby in a hotel, theatre or house
words.mnemonic: Foyer ~ 'four-year' old waits in the lobby.
words.example: We met in the foyer of the theatre before the show.

words.en: very small in amount; relating to a fraction
words.mnemonic: Fraction = a small part; fractional = tiny bit.
words.example: There was only a fractional increase in prices this month.

words.en: a small part broken off or detached
words.mnemonic: Frag(ile) + ment: fragile things break into fragments.
words.example: Archaeologists found fragments of ancient pottery.

words.en: in an open, honest and direct way
words.mnemonic: Frank = honest; Frankly = saaf-saaf bolna.
words.example: Frankly, I don't think your plan will work.

words.en: the killing of one's own brother or sister
words.mnemonic: Frat(ernity) = brother + cide = kill.
words.example: The epic tells of a bloody fratricide between two princes.

words.en: happening often; (verb) to visit a place often
words.mnemonic: Frequent = 'free'-quent: free to come again and again.
words.example: He is a frequent visitor to the library.

words.en: a sudden intense feeling of fear
words.mnemonic: F + right: the right reaction to a ghost is fright.
words.example: The child screamed in fright when the lights went out.

words.en: very cold; showing no warmth of feeling
words.mnemonic: Frigid sounds like fridge: ice cold.
words.example: The explorers survived the frigid Arctic winter.

words.en: a thin layer of ice formed on surfaces in freezing weather
words.mnemonic: Frost = 'frozen' dust on leaves.
words.example: The crops were damaged by an early frost.

words.en: to wrinkle the brow in displeasure or deep thought
words.mnemonic: Frown: the face turns 'down', brows pulled together.
words.example: The teacher frowned at the noisy students.

words.en: the realisation or fulfilment of a plan or project
words.mnemonic: Fruition = tree bears fruit: efforts finally give results.
words.example: After years of hard work, his dream came to fruition.

words.en: forming a necessary base or core; of central importance
words.mnemonic: Fund (base money) + mental: the basic foundation.
words.example: Freedom of speech is a fundamental right.

words.en: a chemical that destroys fungus
words.mnemonic: Fungi + cide (kill) = fungus killer.
words.example: The farmer sprayed fungicide on the wheat crop.

words.en: hard to please; too concerned with small details
words.mnemonic: Fussy person makes a fuss about everything.
words.example: He is very fussy about his food.

words.en: incapable of producing any useful result; pointless
words.mnemonic: Futile ~ 'fu-tile': building a tile house on water is pointless.
words.example: All attempts to save the sinking ship were futile.

words.en: to run or jump about playfully
words.mnemonic: Gambol (not gamble): lambs gambol in the meadow.
words.example: Young lambs were gambolling in the green field.

words.en: a wreath of flowers worn or hung as decoration
words.mnemonic: Garland = 'gale-land': put round the neck (गला).
words.example: The guests were welcomed with garlands of marigold.

words.en: to gather or collect, especially information or support
words.mnemonic: Garner ~ granary: store grain, collect things.
words.example: The film garnered praise from critics across the country.

words.en: to inhale suddenly with the mouth open, from shock or lack of breath
words.mnemonic: Gasp = 'gas' + 'p': gasping for gas (air).
words.example: The audience gasped when the magician vanished.

words.en: to estimate or measure; (noun) a measuring instrument
words.mnemonic: Gauge: 'GAUGE' = Give A Unit, Get Estimate. Note spelling g-a-u-g-e.
words.example: It is difficult to gauge public opinion before the election.

words.en: willing to give more than is necessary; kind and liberal
words.mnemonic: Generous ~ 'general' giving: gives to everyone in general.
words.example: He is generous with his time and money.

words.en: the quality of being kind and willing to give; generosity
words.mnemonic: Generous + ness = the quality of being generous.
words.example: Everyone admired the generousness of the old philanthropist.

words.en: the origin or beginning of something
words.mnemonic: Genesis ~ gene: where life begins.
words.example: The genesis of the idea came from a casual conversation.

words.en: truly what it is said to be; authentic; sincere
words.mnemonic: Genuine = 'gene'-uine: in your genes, so original.
words.example: Is this a genuine diamond or a fake?

words.en: relating to the study of the earth's rocks and structure
words.mnemonic: Geo = earth + logical = study of earth.
words.example: The team carried out a geological survey of the region.

words.en: the science of the earth's physical structure, rocks and history
words.mnemonic: Geo = earth + logy = study.
words.example: She studied geology to understand how mountains are formed.

words.en: a government or state ruled by old people
words.mnemonic: Geronto = old man + cracy = rule.
words.example: Critics described the party leadership as a gerontocracy.

words.en: a movement of the hand or head to express an idea; an act showing feeling
words.mnemonic: Gesture ~ 'just-ure' hands talk: gestures speak without words.
words.example: As a gesture of goodwill, the company donated food.

words.en: to prepare oneself for action; to encircle with a belt
words.mnemonic: Gird = girdle (belt): kamar kasna.
words.example: The soldiers girded themselves for battle.

words.en: a slowly moving mass of ice formed from compacted snow
words.mnemonic: Glacier ~ glass + ice: a river of glassy ice.
words.example: The Gangotri glacier is the source of the Ganga.

words.en: to take a brief or hurried look
words.mnemonic: Glance ~ 'g-lance' (lance = bhala): teer ki tarah ek pal ki nazar.
words.example: She glanced at her watch and hurried out.

words.en: a momentary or partial view
words.mnemonic: Glimpse ~ 'glim'(mer): only a faint flash is seen.
words.example: We caught a glimpse of the actor as his car passed.

words.en: a state of darkness or of sadness and hopelessness
words.mnemonic: Gloom = dark cloud; gloominess = sad darkness.
words.example: The gloominess of the weather matched his mood.

words.en: to praise highly; to make something seem better than it is
words.mnemonic: Glory + fy = to give glory.
words.example: Films should not glorify violence.

words.en: having or bringing great fame; magnificent
words.mnemonic: Glory + ous = full of glory.
words.example: India has a glorious history.

words.en: an alphabetical list of difficult words with their meanings
words.mnemonic: Gloss = explain; glossary explains the hard words.
words.example: Check the glossary at the end of the book for technical terms.

words.en: a mythical dwarf-like creature living underground; a small statue of one
words.mnemonic: Gnome: 'g' silent (NOHM) - bagiche ka chhota bauna.
words.example: There was a stone gnome standing in their garden.

words.en: a person who forms relationships only to get money
words.mnemonic: Digs for gold: wants the partner's money, not love.
words.example: Her friends warned her that he was just a gold-digger.

words.en: elegance of movement; courteous goodwill; divine favour
words.mnemonic: Grace ~ 'grace' marks: given out of kindness.
words.example: She danced with remarkable grace.

words.en: having elegance and beauty of movement or form
words.mnemonic: Grace + ful = full of grace.
words.example: The swan glided across the lake in a graceful manner.

words.en: to arrange in groups by quality or level; to give a mark to
words.mnemonic: Grade A, B, C: arranged by level.
words.example: The eggs are graded according to size.

words.en: slowly, step by step, over a period of time
words.mnemonic: Gradually = grade by grade, step by step.
words.example: The patient's health gradually improved.

words.en: a storehouse for threshed grain
words.mnemonic: Grain + ary = place for grain.
words.example: Punjab is often called the granary of India.

words.en: splendour and impressiveness, especially of appearance or style
words.mnemonic: Grand + eur: grand like a palace.
words.example: Tourists were amazed by the grandeur of the Taj Mahal.

words.en: the quality of being pompous or showily grand; exaggerated self-importance
words.mnemonic: Grand-iose: trying too hard to look grand.
words.example: The grandiosity of his claims made people doubt him.

words.en: to seize and hold firmly; to understand fully
words.mnemonic: Grasp ~ 'grab': grab with the hand or the mind.
words.example: He quickly grasped the main idea of the lesson.

words.en: serious and requiring attention; (noun) a burial place
words.mnemonic: Grave situation is as serious as a grave (क़ब्र).
words.example: The country is facing a grave economic crisis.

words.en: seriously; in a solemn manner
words.mnemonic: Grave + ly = in a grave (serious) way.
words.example: He was gravely injured in the accident.

words.en: a burial ground, especially beside a church
words.mnemonic: Grave + yard = yard full of graves.
words.example: The old graveyard lay behind the church.

words.en: fond of company; sociable; (of animals) living in groups
words.mnemonic: Gregarious ~ 'group-arious': loves to be in groups.
words.example: He is a gregarious person who enjoys parties.

words.en: deep sorrow, especially caused by someone's death
words.mnemonic: Grief ~ 'grieve': you grieve when in grief.
words.example: She was overcome with grief after her father's death.

words.en: an ugly twisted expression of the face showing pain or disgust
words.hi: विकृत मुखमुद्रा, मुँह बिचकाने का भाव
words.mnemonic: Grim + face = grimace.
words.example: He made a grimace as he swallowed the bitter medicine.

words.en: covered with dirt
words.mnemonic: Grime = dirt; grimy = full of grime.
words.example: The mechanic wiped his grimy hands on a cloth.

words.en: to make a deep sound of pain or despair
words.mnemonic: Groan ~ 'grown' man groaning in pain.
words.example: The injured man groaned in pain.

words.en: comically or repulsively ugly or distorted
words.mnemonic: Grotesque ~ grotto monster: strange, ugly shapes.
words.example: The mask had a grotesque face with huge teeth.

words.en: preliminary work that forms a basis for later work
words.mnemonic: Ground + work = work done on the ground level first.
words.example: The meeting laid the groundwork for a peace agreement.

words.en: dirty; unpleasant or disreputable
words.mnemonic: Grubby ~ grub (worm) in dirt.
words.example: The child came home with grubby knees.

words.en: to make a low, short guttural sound, like a pig
