words.example: Hamlet's 'To be or not to be' is a famous soliloquy.

words.en: the state of being alone, often pleasantly
words.mnemonic: Solo + titude: akele rehne ki avastha.
words.example: The poet sought solitude in the mountains.

words.en: a person who talks in his or her sleep
words.mnemonic: Somni (sleep, jaise insomnia) + loqui (speak): neend mein bolne wala.
words.example: My brother is a somniloquist and mumbles all night.

words.en: a person who claims to predict the future
words.mnemonic: Sooth (sach) + sayer: bhavishya ka sach batane wala.
words.example: The soothsayer warned Caesar to beware the Ides of March.

words.en: a person who practises magic, especially black magic
words.mnemonic: Sorcerer ~ 'source of magic' - jaadugar.
words.example: The sorcerer cast a spell on the prince.

words.en: a feeling of deep distress caused by loss or disappointment
words.mnemonic: Sorrow ~ 'sorry' + 'row': gham ki lambi kataar.
words.example: The nation expressed its sorrow at the leader's death.

words.en: a thing kept as a reminder of a person, place or event
words.mnemonic: Souvenir ~ 'sou-venir' (French: yaad) - yaadgaar.
words.example: She bought a small souvenir from Agra.

words.en: possessing supreme or independent authority
words.mnemonic: Sove-reign: jiska apna 'reign' (raj) ho.
words.example: India is a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

words.en: to refrain from harming; to give something that one can afford
words.mnemonic: Spare = 'chhod dena': spare my life!
words.example: The king spared the prisoner's life.

words.en: thinly scattered or distributed
words.mnemonic: Sparse ~ 'spare' - kahin-kahin, bahut kam.
words.example: The desert has sparse vegetation.

words.en: a tiny spot or particle
words.mnemonic: Speck ~ 'spec(s)' par chhota sa dhool ka kan.
words.example: There were specks of dust on the table.

words.en: covered with many small spots
words.mnemonic: Speck (chhota dhabba) + led: chhote-chhote dhabbe.
words.example: The bird laid speckled eggs.

words.en: beautiful in a dramatic and eye-catching way; very impressive
words.mnemonic: Spectacle = drishya; spectacular = dekhne layak.
words.example: The fireworks display was spectacular.

words.en: a person who believes in or claims to communicate with the spirits of the dead
words.mnemonic: Spirit (aatma) + ualist: aatmaon se baat karne wala.
words.example: The spiritualist claimed to contact the dead.

words.en: concern with the human spirit or soul rather than material things
words.mnemonic: Spirit + uality: aatma se juda.
words.example: India is known for its ancient spirituality.

words.en: marked with irregular patches or stains
words.mnemonic: Splotch = bada dhabba; splotchy = dhabbon se bhara.
words.example: Her face became red and splotchy after crying.

words.en: a person who speaks officially on behalf of a group or organisation
words.mnemonic: Spoke (bola) + person: jo sabki taraf se bole.
words.example: The party spokesperson denied the allegations.

words.en: false or fake; not genuine; based on wrong reasoning
words.mnemonic: Spurious ~ 'spur-ious': nakli maal - spurious liquor.
words.example: The court dismissed the spurious claims.

words.en: a short, high-pitched sound or cry
words.mnemonic: Squeak - chuhe ki 'chee-chee' awaaz.
words.example: The door opened with a squeak.

words.en: firmly fixed; not likely to change or fail
words.mnemonic: Stable ~ 'table' jaisa - hilta nahi.
words.example: The patient's condition is now stable.

words.en: no longer fresh; lacking originality
words.mnemonic: Stale ~ 'stall' par pada purana khana - baasi.
words.example: The bread had gone stale.

words.en: a person who secretly follows and harasses someone
words.mnemonic: Stalk = chupke se peechha karna.
words.example: The police arrested the stalker who had been following her.

words.en: the ability to sustain prolonged physical or mental effort
words.mnemonic: Stamina ~ 'stay + man': der tak tike rehne ki shakti.
words.example: Marathon runners need great stamina.

words.en: main or most important, especially of food or a product
words.mnemonic: Staple food = rozana ka mukhya khana (chawal, roti).
words.example: Rice is the staple food of Bengal.

words.en: not moving; still (not 'stationery' = writing materials)
words.mnemonic: Station-ARY: train stAtion par rukti hai - A for 'At rest'.
words.example: The truck crashed into a stationary car.

words.en: free from germs; unable to produce offspring or crops
words.mnemonic: Sterile ~ 'steril-ise': operation ke auzaar kitanu-rahit.
words.example: Surgeons use sterile instruments.

words.en: serious and strict, especially in demanding discipline
words.mnemonic: Stern ~ 'stone' jaisa sakht chehra.
words.example: The teacher gave the boys a stern warning.

words.en: the quality of being serious and strict
words.mnemonic: Stern + ness = sakhti.
words.example: The sternness in his voice silenced the class.

words.en: a substance or thing that increases activity or energy
words.mnemonic: Stimulant = 'stimulate' karne wala - chai-coffee jaisa jo body ko jaga de
words.example: Caffeine is a mild stimulant found in tea and coffee.

words.en: encouraging interest, thought or activity; exciting
words.mnemonic: Stimulating discussion = dimag ko 'stimulate' (jagaane) wali
words.example: We had a stimulating discussion on climate change.

words.en: enduring pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining
words.mnemonic: Stoic = 'stone-ic' - patthar jaisa, dard mein bhi chehra bhavheen
words.example: She remained stoic throughout the long illness.

words.en: to bend the body forwards and downwards
words.mnemonic: Stoop = 'stool' par baithne ke liye jhukna
words.example: The old man stooped to pick up the coin.

words.en: a narrow passage of water connecting two large seas; (straits) difficulty
words.mnemonic: Strait = 'straight' narrow raasta paani ka - Palk Strait yaad rakho
words.example: The Palk Strait separates India from Sri Lanka.

words.en: strict, precise and exacting (of rules or conditions)
words.mnemonic: Stringent = 'string' tight kheenchi hui - bahut sakht niyam
words.example: The government introduced stringent laws against pollution.

words.en: determined not to change one's attitude or position; obstinate
words.mnemonic: Stubborn = 'stub' (thooth) jaisa adiyal - hilta hi nahi
words.example: The stubborn child refused to eat his vegetables.

words.en: to bring under domination or control, especially by conquest
words.mnemonic: Sub (neeche) + jugate (yoke = jua) - jue ke neeche laana = gulaam banana
words.example: The empire tried to subjugate the neighbouring tribes.

words.en: ready to obey others without resistance
words.mnemonic: Submissive = 'submit' kar dene wala - turant jhuk jaata hai
words.example: The dog became submissive in front of its master.

words.en: a written order requiring a person to attend a court
words.mnemonic: Sub + poena (penalty) - court ka order, na aaye to penalty
words.example: The witness received a subpoena to appear in court.

words.en: coming after something in time; following
words.mnemonic: Sub-sequent = sequence mein baad wala
words.example: Subsequent events proved him right.

words.en: to become less intense, violent or severe; to sink lower
words.mnemonic: Subside = 'sub' (neeche) baith jaana - toofan dheere-dheere neeche
words.example: The floodwaters began to subside after a week.

words.en: relating to regions bordering the tropics
words.mnemonic: Sub (lagbhag) + tropical = tropics ke paas ka ilaka
words.example: Florida has a subtropical climate.

words.en: following one after another without interruption
words.mnemonic: Successive = 'success' ke baad success - ek ke baad ek
words.example: The team won three successive matches.

words.en: help and support in times of difficulty
words.mnemonic: Succour sounds like 'sahara' - mushkil mein madad
words.example: The Red Cross gave succour to the flood victims.

words.en: enough; as much as is needed
words.mnemonic: Sufficient = 'suffice' karna - kaafi hai
words.example: We have sufficient food for the journey.

words.en: a set of connected rooms; a set of matching furniture or things
words.mnemonic: Suite (sweet) - hotel ka 'sweet' set of rooms
words.example: The minister stayed in the presidential suite of the hotel.

words.en: to officially order someone to come; to call upon
words.mnemonic: Summon = 'samman' (court ka summons) bhej kar bulana
words.example: The principal summoned the students to his office.

words.en: behaving as though one is superior to others; arrogant
words.mnemonic: Super + cilia (bhaun/eyebrow) - bhaunhein upar karke dekhne wala ghamandi
words.example: He gave a supercilious smile and ignored the question.

words.en: existing only on the surface; not thorough or deep
words.mnemonic: Super (upar) + ficial (face) - sirf upari surface
words.example: He has only a superficial knowledge of history.

words.en: of the highest quality or degree; excellent
words.mnemonic: Superlative = super se bhi upar - best, highest
words.example: The actor gave a superlative performance.

words.en: to take the place of something older or less useful; replace
words.mnemonic: Super (upar) + sede (seat) - purane ki seat par upar baith jaana
words.example: The new rules will supersede the old ones.

words.en: having irrational beliefs in luck, magic or omens
words.mnemonic: Superstitious = billi raasta kaate to ruk jaane wala
words.example: He is so superstitious that he never travels on Saturdays.

words.en: to observe and direct the work of others
words.mnemonic: Super (upar) + vise (dekhna) - upar se dekhna
words.example: A senior engineer will supervise the construction.

words.en: added to complete or improve something; additional
words.mnemonic: Supplement = poorak - extra joda gaya
words.example: The government passed a supplementary budget.

words.en: in a way that gives help or encouragement
words.mnemonic: Support + ively = sahara dete hue
words.example: Her teacher nodded supportively as she spoke.

words.en: to forcibly put an end to; to hold back or conceal
words.mnemonic: Sup (neeche) + press (dabana) = neeche daba dena
words.example: The army was sent to suppress the rebellion.

words.en: able to be overcome
words.mnemonic: Sur (upar) + mount (pahaad) - pahaad jis par chadha ja sake
words.example: These problems are difficult but surmountable.

words.en: an amount left over when requirements are met; excess
words.mnemonic: Sur (upar) + plus = zaroorat se upar extra
words.example: India has a surplus of wheat this year.

words.en: to stop resisting and give in to an enemy or authority
words.mnemonic: Sur-ender = ladai ka 'end' karke haath upar
words.example: The rebels were forced to surrender.

words.en: done secretly to avoid notice
words.mnemonic: Surreptitious = 'sar-rap-chhupa' - chupke-chupke kiya gaya
words.example: She cast a surreptitious glance at her phone during the meeting.

words.en: close observation, especially of a suspected person
words.mnemonic: Sur (upar) + veil (parda) - parde ke peechhe se upar se nazar rakhna
words.example: The suspect was kept under police surveillance.

words.en: the state of being easily affected or harmed by something
words.mnemonic: Susceptible + ity = jaldi asar hone ki kshamata
words.example: Old age increases susceptibility to infections.

words.en: likely to be influenced or harmed by something
words.mnemonic: Susceptible = 'sus' (suspect) jo turant pakad mein aa jaye
words.example: Children are more susceptible to colds.

words.en: to believe something to be true or someone guilty without proof
words.mnemonic: Suspect = shak - 'sus' bolte hain shak ke liye
words.example: The police suspected the servant of theft.

words.en: having or causing a feeling that something is wrong
words.mnemonic: Suspicious = suspect jaisa - shak paida karne wala
words.example: A suspicious bag was found at the station.

words.en: continuing for a long period without interruption
words.mnemonic: Sustain = tikana - lambe samay tak tika hua
words.example: Success requires sustained effort.

words.en: to make food or drink pass down the throat; to accept without question
words.mnemonic: Swallow = 'swaa-low' - gale se neeche le jaana
words.example: He swallowed the tablet with a glass of water.

words.en: to make a solemn promise; to use offensive language
words.hi: शपथ लेना, कसम खाना; गाली देना
words.mnemonic: Swear - swore - sworn: 'sworn statement' = kasam kha kar diya bayaan
words.example: Witnesses must swear to tell the truth.

words.en: wide in range or effect; too general
words.mnemonic: Sweeping = jhaadu ki tarah sab kuchh samet lena
words.example: The new government made sweeping changes to the tax system.

words.en: to hit with a swinging movement; to move a finger across a screen or card
words.mnemonic: Swipe card - card ko jhatke se sarkaana
words.example: Swipe left to see the next photo.

words.en: larger than normal, especially due to fluid or injury
words.mnemonic: Swollen = 'swell' hua - sooj gaya
words.example: His ankle was swollen after the fall.

words.en: a person who flatters powerful people to gain advantage
words.mnemonic: Sycophant = 'sick-o-fan' - boss ka beemar fan jo chamchagiri kare
words.example: The king was surrounded by sycophants.

words.en: the use of symbols to represent ideas or qualities
words.mnemonic: Symbol + ism = prateekon ka prayog
words.example: The poem is rich in religious symbolism.

words.en: made artificially by chemical processes; not natural
words.mnemonic: Synthetic = 'sin-thetic' - lab mein bana, nakli
words.example: Nylon is a synthetic fibre.

words.en: reserved or saying very little; habitually silent
words.mnemonic: Taciturn = 'tacit' (mauna) + turn - bolne ki turn hi nahi leta
words.example: My taciturn neighbour rarely says more than hello.

words.en: actions planned carefully to achieve a specific end
words.mnemonic: Tactics = 'tact' se chaalein chalna
words.example: The team changed its tactics in the second half.

words.en: fond of talking a lot
words.mnemonic: Talk + ative = baatein karne ka shauqeen
words.example: The talkative student was asked to keep quiet.

words.en: to interfere with something in order to cause damage or make changes
words.mnemonic: Tamper = 'temper' kharab karke chhed-chhaad
words.example: Someone had tampered with the evidence.

words.en: perceptible by touch; clear and definite; real
words.mnemonic: Tangible = 'tang' (touch) karne layak
words.example: The new policy has produced tangible results.

words.en: a person who prepares and stuffs the skins of dead animals to look lifelike
words.hi: मृत पशुओं में भूसा भरने वाला
words.mnemonic: Taxi (arrange) + derm (skin) = khaal sajaane wala
words.example: The taxidermist mounted the tiger's head on a wall.

words.en: a person's nature, especially as it affects their behaviour
words.mnemonic: Temper + ament = insaan ka temper yaani mizaaj
words.example: He has a calm temperament.

words.en: lasting for only a limited period
words.mnemonic: Temporary = 'tempo' ki sawari - thodi der ki
words.example: He got a temporary job during the holidays.

words.en: the quality of being very determined; persistence
words.mnemonic: Tenacity = 'ten' baar haar kar bhi 'city' jeetne ki zid
words.example: Her tenacity helped her clear the exam on the fourth attempt.

words.en: a person who rents land or property from a landlord
words.mnemonic: Tenant = 'ten' (rakhna) - jo ghar kiraye par rakhe
words.example: The landlord asked the tenants to pay the rent on time.

words.en: an inclination towards a particular behaviour or characteristic
words.mnemonic: Tendency = 'tend' karna yaani jhukna kisi or
words.example: He has a tendency to exaggerate.

words.en: not certain or fixed; provisional; hesitant
words.mnemonic: Tentative = 'tent' jaisa - kabhi bhi ukhad sakta hai, pakka nahi
words.example: We made a tentative plan to meet on Sunday.

words.en: to bring to an end
words.mnemonic: Terminate = 'Terminator' sab khatam kar deta hai
words.example: The company terminated his contract.

words.en: a person who believes in the existence of God
words.mnemonic: Theos = God; theist = God ko maanne wala (opposite: atheist)
words.example: As a theist, he prays every morning.

words.en: an expert in the study of religion and God
words.mnemonic: Theo (God) + logy (study) = dharm ka gyaani
words.example: The theologian wrote a book on ancient scriptures.

words.en: based on theory rather than practice
words.mnemonic: Theory + tical = kitaabi, practical nahi
words.example: He has theoretical knowledge but no practical experience.

words.en: a person who forms theories about a subject
words.mnemonic: Theory + ist = theory banane wala
words.example: Marx was a famous political theorist.

words.en: a book that lists words grouped by similar meanings
words.mnemonic: Thesaurus = 'treasure' of words - synonyms ka khazana
words.example: Use a thesaurus to find a better word.

words.en: using money and resources carefully; economical
words.mnemonic: Thrifty = 'thrift' (bachat) + fifty paise bhi bachaye
words.example: His thrifty habits helped him buy a house.

words.en: to prevent someone from accomplishing something
words.mnemonic: Thwart = 'thwack' maarkar plan rok dena
words.example: The police thwarted the robbery attempt.

words.en: lacking courage or confidence; easily frightened
words.mnemonic: Timid = 'time' par bhi bol na sake, darpok
words.example: The timid boy hid behind his mother.

words.en: lack of courage or confidence
words.mnemonic: Timid + ity = darpokpan
words.example: His timidity stopped him from asking questions.

words.en: willingness to accept views or behaviour different from one's own; endurance
words.mnemonic: Tolerate = sehna; tolerance = sehne ki shakti
words.example: Religious tolerance is essential in a diverse society.

words.en: a large grave, often with a monument over it
words.mnemonic: Tomb (toom) - Humayun ka Tomb = maqbara
words.example: The Taj Mahal is a tomb built by Shah Jahan.

words.en: a stone slab marking a grave, with the name of the dead person
words.mnemonic: Tomb + stone = kabr par laga pathar
words.example: His name was carved on the tombstone.

words.en: mentally or physically inactive; sluggish
words.mnemonic: Torpid = 'tor-pede' - pair toote jaise sust
words.example: The heat made everyone feel torpid.

words.en: a strong, fast-moving stream of water or of words
words.mnemonic: Torrent = 'tor-rent' - baadh ka tez paani sab tod de
words.example: The rain fell in torrents all night.

words.en: the act of causing severe pain as punishment or to force information
words.mnemonic: Torture = 'tod-ture' - haddi tod dene wala dard
words.example: The prisoners were subjected to torture.

words.en: a mark or sign left behind; a very small amount
words.mnemonic: Trace = traces (nishaan) dhoondhna
words.example: The thief disappeared without a trace.

words.en: a person who betrays their country, friends or principles
words.mnemonic: Traitor = 'trade-or' - desh ko bech (trade) dene wala
words.example: He was branded a traitor for selling secrets.

words.en: a person who travels on foot from place to place, homeless; a long walk
words.mnemonic: Tramp = 'tram' ke bina paidal ghoomne wala
words.example: A tramp was sleeping on the park bench.

words.en: the quality of being calm and peaceful
words.mnemonic: Tranquil = 'tran-kill' - shor ko kill karke shanti
words.example: We enjoyed the tranquility of the hills.

words.en: the quality of being calm and peaceful (British spelling)
words.mnemonic: Double L = double shanti (British spelling)
words.example: The tranquillity of the lake was broken by a speedboat.

words.en: to make a thorough change in form, appearance or character
words.mnemonic: Trans (paar) + form (roop) = roop badal dena
words.example: Education can transform a person's life.

words.en: a complete change in form or appearance
words.mnemonic: Transformers movie - gaadi robot mein badal jaati hai
words.example: The city has undergone a complete transformation.

words.en: not permanent; lasting only a short time
words.mnemonic: Transit = guzarna; transitory = guzar jaane wala
words.example: Fame is often transitory.

words.en: allowing light through so objects can be seen; open and honest
words.mnemonic: Trans (aar-paar) + parent (dikhna) = aar-paar dikhne wala
words.example: The government promised a transparent recruitment process.

words.en: a great victory or achievement
words.mnemonic: Triumph = 'trophy' jeetne ki khushi
words.example: The election result was a triumph for democracy.

words.en: of little value or importance
words.mnemonic: Trivial = tri (teen) + via (raaste) - chauraahe ki mamuli baat
words.example: Don't waste time on trivial matters.

words.en: a student who stays away from school without permission
words.mnemonic: Truant = 'true aunt' ke ghar jaane ka bahana karke school se bhaagna
words.example: The truant was caught playing in the park.

words.en: to move slowly and heavily on wheels
words.mnemonic: Trundle = 'trunk' ko pahiyon par dheere ghaseetna
words.example: The old bus trundled along the dusty road.

words.en: violent or unsteady movement of air or water; conflict
words.mnemonic: Turbulence - flight mein jhatke = turbine jaisa ghoomta hawa
words.example: The plane hit some turbulence over the mountains.

words.en: swollen; (of language) pompous and boring
words.mnemonic: Turgid = 'tur' (bhara) + gid - phoola hua, bhaari bhaasha
words.example: The report was written in turgid prose.

words.en: to turn or bend into a different shape; to distort the meaning of
words.mnemonic: Twist dance - kamar ko marodna
words.example: Don't twist my words.

words.en: a violent tropical storm in the western Pacific
words.mnemonic: Typhoon sounds like 'toofan'
words.example: The typhoon caused heavy damage in the Philippines.

words.en: a cruel and oppressive ruler
words.mnemonic: Tyrant = 'tyre' se kuchal dene wala shasak
words.example: The people rose up against the tyrant.

words.en: being the final or best of its kind
words.mnemonic: Ultimate = 'ultra' last - sabse aakhri
words.example: Our ultimate goal is to win the championship.

words.en: not recognised or given credit
words.hi: उपेक्षित, जिसे श्रेय या मान्यता न मिली हो
words.mnemonic: Un + acknowledge = jiska credit na diya gaya
words.example: Her contribution to the project went unacknowledged.

words.en: to open by drawing back a bolt
words.mnemonic: Un + bolt = kundi khol di
words.example: He unbolted the door and stepped outside.

words.en: to experience or be subjected to something unpleasant or difficult
words.mnemonic: Under + go = mushkil ke neeche se guzarna
words.example: He will undergo surgery next week.

words.en: to commit oneself to and begin a task
words.mnemonic: Under + take = kaam apne haath mein lena
words.example: The company will undertake the construction of the bridge.

words.en: a task or project, especially a difficult one; a formal promise
words.mnemonic: Undertake ka kaam = undertaking
words.example: Building the dam was a massive undertaking.

words.en: not recognised or identified
words.mnemonic: Un + identified = jiski pehchaan na ho (UFO = Unidentified Flying Object)
words.example: An unidentified man was seen near the building.

words.en: to release or set free something powerful
words.mnemonic: Un + leash (patta) = kutte ka patta khol dena
words.example: The storm unleashed its fury on the coast.

words.en: not controlled or supervised by rules
words.mnemonic: Un + regulated = bina niyam ke
words.example: Unregulated mining has damaged the forests.

words.en: impossible to stop or prevent
words.hi: अजेय, जिसे रोका न जा सके
words.mnemonic: Un + stop + able = jise roka na ja sake
words.example: The team seemed unstoppable this season.

words.en: not spoiled or made impure; spotless
words.mnemonic: Sully = gandaa karna; unsullied = bina daag
words.example: He retired with an unsullied reputation.

words.en: not able to be relied on as honest or truthful
words.mnemonic: Un + trust + worthy = bharose ke laayak nahi
words.example: Never share secrets with an untrustworthy person.

words.en: not ready or eager to do something
words.mnemonic: Un + willing = man nahi hai
words.example: He was unwilling to admit his mistake.

words.en: not giving way to pressure; firm or inflexible
words.mnemonic: Yield = jhukna; unyielding = na jhukne wala
words.example: She faced the problem with unyielding courage.

words.en: erect or vertical; strictly honest
words.mnemonic: Up + right = seedha upar khada aur sahi (imaandaar)
words.example: He is an upright officer who never takes bribes.

words.en: importance requiring swift action
words.mnemonic: Urgent + cy = jaldi ki zaroorat
words.example: The doctor stressed the urgency of the operation.

words.en: requiring immediate action or attention
words.mnemonic: Urgent = 'ur-jaldi' - abhi chahiye
words.example: I have an urgent message for the manager.

words.en: a doctor who specialises in the urinary system
words.mnemonic: Uro (urine) + logist = mootra ka doctor
words.example: He consulted a urologist about his kidney stone.

words.en: the branch of medicine dealing with the urinary system
words.mnemonic: Uro (urine) + logy (study)
words.example: She works in the urology department of the hospital.

words.en: to show or guide someone somewhere; to mark the start of something
words.hi: ले जाना, अगुवाई करना, शुरुआत करना
words.mnemonic: Usher = 'us-her' ko seat tak le jaana
words.example: The internet ushered in a new era of communication.

words.en: to take a position of power illegally or by force
words.mnemonic: Usurp = 'U-sirf' - mera hak zabardasti chheen liya
words.example: The general tried to usurp the throne.

words.en: the state of being useful; a useful service such as electricity or water
words.mnemonic: Utility = use + ility = upyog
words.example: Electricity and water are public utilities.

words.en: an imagined place where everything is perfect
words.mnemonic: U-topia = 'no place' - aisi jagah jo hai hi nahi, ram-rajya
words.example: The writer described a utopia without poverty or crime.

words.en: to say something or make a sound with the voice
words.mnemonic: Utter = 'uttar' dena - munh se bolna
words.example: He left without uttering a single word.

words.en: not occupied; empty; (of a look) showing no thought
words.mnemonic: Vacant = 'vacate' kiya hua, khaali
words.example: There are three vacant posts in the office.

words.en: to leave a place or position, making it empty
words.mnemonic: Vacate = vacation par ghar khaali karna
words.example: The tenants vacated the flat last month.

words.en: a person without a home or job who wanders from place to place
words.mnemonic: Vagrant = 'vague' raaste par bhatakne wala
words.example: The vagrant slept under the bridge.

words.en: in a way that is uncertain or unclear
words.hi: अस्पष्ट रूप से, धुँधले रूप से
words.mnemonic: Vague = dhundhla; vaguely = dhundhla sa
words.example: I vaguely remember meeting him years ago.

words.en: to check or prove the accuracy or worth of something; to make legally acceptable
words.mnemonic: Valid + ate = valid (maanya) banana
words.example: The experiment validated his theory.

words.en: great force or strength of feeling
words.mnemonic: Vehemence = 'vahan' ki tez speed jaisi zor ki bhavna
words.example: She denied the charges with great vehemence.

words.en: deserving great respect because of age, wisdom or character
words.mnemonic: Venerable = 'venerate' (poojna) karne laayak buzurg
words.example: The venerable monk blessed the visitors.

words.en: a performer who speaks without moving the lips, so the voice seems to come from a puppet
words.hi: कठपुतली के लिए आवाज़ बदलकर बोलने वाला
words.mnemonic: Ventri (pet) + loqui (bolna) = pet se bolne wala
words.example: The ventriloquist made his puppet sing a song.

words.en: using more words than needed
words.mnemonic: Verb + ose = bahut zyada 'verbs'/words
words.example: His verbose speech bored the audience.

words.en: able to adapt to many different functions or activities
words.mnemonic: Versatile = 'vers' (turn) - har taraf mud jaane wala, all-rounder
words.example: Amitabh Bachchan is a versatile actor.

words.en: a ship or large boat; a container for liquids; a tube in the body
words.mnemonic: Vessel = 'vasal' - bartan; blood vessel = khoon ki nali
words.example: The fishing vessel returned to the harbour.

words.en: a person with long experience in a field; a former soldier
words.mnemonic: Veteran = 'vet' + 'ran' - bahut saal se daud raha anubhavi
words.example: The veteran journalist has covered ten elections.

words.en: the state of being full of energy and life
words.mnemonic: Vibrant = jeevant; vibrancy = jeevantata
words.example: The festival added vibrancy to the city.

words.en: a person who defeats an opponent; a winner
words.mnemonic: Victor = victory paane wala
words.example: History is written by the victors.

words.en: physical strength and good health; energy
words.mnemonic: Vigour = 'vigorous' - full energy
words.example: He started his new job with great vigour.

words.en: extremely unpleasant; morally bad; wicked
words.mnemonic: Vile = 'vile-n' (villain) jaisa ghatiya
words.example: Murder is a vile crime.

words.en: of high quality and lasting value; old but classic
words.mnemonic: Vintage car = purani magar shaandaar
words.example: He collects vintage cars.

words.en: the act of breaking a law, rule or agreement
words.mnemonic: Violate = todna; violation = niyam todna
words.example: The factory was fined for safety violations.

words.en: almost or nearly as described; existing in computer form
words.mnemonic: Virtual reality = asli jaisa par asli nahi
words.example: The project came to a virtual standstill.

words.en: having high moral standards
words.mnemonic: Virtue = sadgun; virtuous = sadguno wala
words.example: He led a virtuous life.

words.en: able to be seen
words.mnemonic: Vis = dekhna (vision) - jo dikhe
words.example: The stars are clearly visible tonight.

words.en: a person with original ideas about the future
words.mnemonic: Vision + ary = aage ka dekhne wala
words.example: Visionaries like Dr Kalam inspired a generation.

words.en: absolutely necessary; essential for life
words.mnemonic: Vital = 'vita' (life) - jeevan ke liye zaroori
words.example: Water is vital for survival.

words.en: the body's important organs; basic signs of life such as pulse
words.mnemonic: Vitals = vital (zaroori) angon ki jaanch
words.example: The nurse checked the patient's vitals.

words.en: to spoil or impair the quality of; to make legally invalid
words.mnemonic: Vitiate = 'vish' (zeher) daalna - kharab kar dena
words.example: Smoke from factories vitiates the air.

words.en: a person's occupation, especially one they feel strongly suited to
words.mnemonic: Vocation = 'voice' (call) - mann ki pukaar wala kaam
words.example: Teaching is not just a job but a vocation for her.

words.en: the prevailing fashion or style at a particular time
words.mnemonic: Vogue magazine = fashion; 'in vogue' = chalan mein
words.example: Short hair is in vogue these days.

words.en: exposed to being attacked or harmed
words.mnemonic: Vulner (zakhm) + able = jise aasani se chot lage
words.example: Children and old people are most vulnerable to the virus.

words.en: an official document authorising an action such as an arrest; justification
words.mnemonic: Warrant - police arrest warrant leke aati hai
words.example: The police obtained a warrant to search the house.

words.en: using more of something than necessary; extravagant
words.mnemonic: Waste + ful = barbaad karne wala
words.example: It is wasteful to leave the lights on all day.

words.en: a person employed to guard a building, especially at night
words.mnemonic: Watch + man = dekhrekh karne wala aadmi
words.example: The watchman locked the gate at midnight.

words.en: to be undecided between choices; to move unsteadily
words.mnemonic: Waver = 'wave' jaisa idhar-udhar dolna
words.example: Her support for the plan never wavered.

words.en: to make or become weaker
words.mnemonic: Weak + en = kamzor banana
words.example: Illness had weakened his body.

words.en: in contrast or comparison with the fact that
words.mnemonic: Whereas = jahan ek taraf... wahin doosri taraf
words.example: Some people love winter, whereas others prefer summer.

words.en: by which; by means of which
words.mnemonic: Where + by = jiske dwara
words.example: They set up a system whereby people could pay online.

words.en: in which; in what respect
words.mnemonic: Where + in = jiske andar
words.example: This is the room wherein the treaty was signed.

words.en: of what or of which (formal)
words.mnemonic: Where + of = jiske baare mein
words.example: He knows whereof he speaks.

words.en: playfully unusual; acting on sudden fancies
words.mnemonic: Whim = sanak; whimsical = sanak par chalne wala
words.example: The book has a whimsical sense of humour.

words.en: a wild, uncultivated and uninhabited region
words.mnemonic: Wild + er + ness = jungli, veeran ilaka
words.example: They were lost in the wilderness for three days.

words.en: intentional; deliberate; stubborn and determined to do as one wants
words.mnemonic: Will (iccha) + ful = apni marzi se, jaanbujh kar (British spelling: wilful)
words.example: He was charged with willful damage to property.

words.en: to remove or take back; to leave or retreat
words.mnemonic: With + draw = kheench kar wapas lena
words.example: He withdrew money from the bank.

words.en: very shy and quiet; not wanting to communicate with others
words.mnemonic: Withdrawn = khud ko duniya se 'withdraw' kar liya
words.example: After the accident, he became quiet and withdrawn.

words.en: to remain undamaged by; to resist successfully
words.mnemonic: With + stand = khilaaf khade rehna
words.example: The building can withstand earthquakes.

words.en: a person who sees an event take place; one who gives evidence in court
words.mnemonic: Witness = 'wit' (jaanna) - jo jaanta/dekhta hai
words.example: The witness described the accident to the police.

words.en: the organ in a woman's body where a baby develops; uterus
words.mnemonic: Womb = 'woman' ke andar bachche ka ghar
words.example: The baby grows in the mother's womb for nine months.

words.en: to show deep respect and love for a god; to adore
words.mnemonic: Worship = 'war-ship' nahi, 'worth-ship' - jo worth ho uski pooja
words.example: Hindus worship many gods and goddesses.

words.en: having no real value or use
words.mnemonic: Worth + less = koi keemat nahi
words.example: The old coins turned out to be worthless.

words.en: to cover, surround or encircle
words.mnemonic: Wreath = phoolon ki maala; wreathe = maala se gher dena
words.example: Her face was wreathed in smiles.

words.en: great energy or enthusiasm for a cause or objective
words.mnemonic: Zeal = 'jeel' - jeetne ka jazba
words.example: He worked with great zeal for the poor.

words.en: the highest point; the time of greatest success
words.mnemonic: Zenith = 'Z' last letter - sabse upar ka point
words.example: The empire reached its zenith under Akbar.

words.en: the scientific study of animals
words.mnemonic: Zoo + logy = jaanwaron ka adhyayan
words.example: She is doing a master's degree in zoology.

idioms.en: a new person in charge makes many changes
idioms.hi: नया मुल्ला ज़्यादा प्याज़ खाता है; नया अधिकारी बड़े बदलाव करता है
idioms.mnemonic: A new broom cleans thoroughly at first.
idioms.example: The new principal changed every rule; a new broom sweeps clean.

idioms.word: a stitch in time saves nine
idioms.en: timely action prevents bigger trouble later
idioms.hi: समय पर किया गया काम बाद की परेशानी बचाता है
idioms.mnemonic: One stitch now saves nine stitches later.
idioms.example: Repair the leak today; a stitch in time saves nine.

idioms.en: a weak or vulnerable point
idioms.mnemonic: Greek hero Achilles could be wounded only at his heel.
idioms.example: Poor spelling is his Achilles' heel in exams.

idioms.en: what you do matters more than what you say
idioms.mnemonic: Deeds are louder than talk.
idioms.example: Stop promising and start helping; actions speak louder than words.

idioms.en: having full authority; supreme (also: considering everything)
idioms.mnemonic: 'All' things are 'in' the hands of one 'all'-powerful person.
idioms.example: In this office the director is all in all.

idioms.en: a cause of quarrel or dispute
idioms.mnemonic: Greek myth: a golden apple caused the quarrel that led to the Trojan War.
idioms.example: The ancestral land became the apple of discord between the brothers.

idioms.en: a person who is very dear
idioms.mnemonic: Like the pupil of the eye, something you protect most.
idioms.example: The youngest grandson is the apple of his grandmother's eye.

idioms.en: to be perfectly neat and well arranged
idioms.hi: पूरी तरह व्यवस्थित और साफ़-सुथरा होना
idioms.mnemonic: Picture apple slices laid in perfect rows on a pie.
idioms.example: Before the inspection, every file was in apple-pie order.

idioms.en: to share the same understanding or agreement
idioms.mnemonic: Everyone reading the same page of the book.
idioms.example: Let's meet once more to make sure we are all on the same page.

idioms.en: to run away; withdraw hastily
idioms.mnemonic: Armies once beat drums to signal a retreat.
idioms.example: The thieves beat a retreat when the dogs started barking.

idioms.word: beauty is in the eye of the beholder
idioms.en: beauty is a matter of personal opinion
idioms.hi: सुंदरता देखने वाले की आँखों में होती है
idioms.mnemonic: Beholder = the one who looks; beauty depends on him.
idioms.example: You may not like the painting, but beauty is in the eye of the beholder.

idioms.en: in one's absence; secretly
idioms.mnemonic: Things done where you cannot see them.
idioms.example: It is mean to criticise your friends behind their backs.

idioms.en: to undertake a dangerous or very difficult task
idioms.hi: जोखिम भरा काम अपने सिर लेना
idioms.mnemonic: Fable: mice wanted a bell on the cat, but none dared tie it.
idioms.example: Everyone complained about the boss, but no one would bell the cat.

idioms.en: to face a painful or unpleasant situation bravely
idioms.hi: कठिन परिस्थिति का साहस से सामना करना
idioms.mnemonic: Soldiers bit a bullet to bear pain during surgery without anaesthesia.
idioms.example: She bit the bullet and went ahead with the surgery.

idioms.en: to praise oneself; boast
idioms.mnemonic: Playing your own trumpet to announce your greatness.
idioms.example: A truly talented person rarely needs to blow his own trumpet.

idioms.en: to amount to; be reduced to its essence
idioms.mnemonic: Boiling a liquid leaves only the essence behind.
idioms.example: The whole dispute boils down to a lack of trust.

idioms.en: to make a start by easing initial shyness or tension
idioms.hi: झिझक दूर करना; बातचीत शुरू करना
idioms.mnemonic: Ships broke ice to open a route for others.
idioms.example: The host told a joke to break the ice at the meeting.

idioms.en: someone or something new and refreshing
idioms.mnemonic: Like fresh air in a stuffy room.
idioms.example: The new teacher's lively style was a breath of fresh air for the class.

idioms.en: to punish someone or make them answer for their actions
idioms.mnemonic: The culprit's name is written in the 'book' of justice.
idioms.example: The corrupt officials must be brought to book.

idioms.en: to raise or mention a topic
idioms.mnemonic: Bring a topic 'up' to the table.
idioms.example: She brought up an important point during the discussion.

idioms.en: to have unrealistic dreams or plans
idioms.hi: हवाई किले बनाना; शेखचिल्ली के सपने देखना
idioms.mnemonic: A castle in the air has no foundation.
idioms.example: Instead of building castles in the air, prepare a practical plan.

idioms.en: to end a quarrel and make peace
idioms.mnemonic: Native Americans buried their hatchets (axes) to declare peace.
idioms.example: After years of rivalry, the two neighbours buried the hatchet.

idioms.en: very rapidly
idioms.hi: तेज़ी से; दिन दूनी रात चौगुनी
idioms.mnemonic: Progress that leaps and jumps instead of walking.
idioms.example: Her confidence has grown by leaps and bounds.

idioms.word: by the skin of one's teeth
idioms.en: by a very narrow margin; barely
idioms.mnemonic: Teeth have no skin; the margin was that thin.
idioms.example: He passed the exam by the skin of his teeth.

idioms.en: to stop working for the time being
idioms.hi: काम बंद करना; दिन का काम समाप्त करना
idioms.mnemonic: Declare the working day over.
idioms.example: We have worked for ten hours; let's call it a day.

idioms.en: to be in charge; make the decisions
idioms.mnemonic: The one who decides which shots to fire.
idioms.example: In this company, the founder still calls the shots.

idioms.en: to win; be successful
idioms.mnemonic: Carry away the victory of the day's battle.
idioms.example: Her brilliant argument carried the day in the debate.

idioms.en: to damage someone's reputation
idioms.mnemonic: Slur = stain; throwing a stain on someone's name.
idioms.example: The false rumours cast a slur on his honesty.

idioms.en: a difficult situation from which there is no escape because of contradictory conditions
idioms.hi: दुविधा की स्थिति जिसमें कोई हल संभव न हो
idioms.mnemonic: From Joseph Heller's novel 'Catch-22'.
idioms.example: No job without experience, no experience without a job: it's a Catch-22.

idioms.en: to chat casually; gossip
idioms.mnemonic: Like chewing something slowly and endlessly while talking.
idioms.example: The old friends sat on the porch chewing the fat.

idioms.en: a person who resembles a parent in character or behaviour
idioms.hi: बाप पर गया बेटा; जैसा बाप वैसा बेटा
idioms.mnemonic: A chip cut from a block is made of the same wood.
idioms.example: With his love of music, the boy is a chip off the old block.

idioms.en: to become silent suddenly
idioms.mnemonic: A clam shuts its shell tightly.
idioms.example: He clammed up when the police asked about the money.

idioms.en: to become known; be revealed
idioms.mnemonic: Something hidden in the dark comes into the light.
idioms.example: New facts about the scam came to light during the inquiry.

idioms.en: very calm and composed
idioms.mnemonic: A cucumber stays cool inside even on a hot day.
idioms.example: Despite the pressure, the captain remained cool as a cucumber.

idioms.word: cost an arm and a leg
idioms.en: to be very expensive
idioms.mnemonic: So costly that you pay with your limbs.
idioms.example: The trip to Europe cost us an arm and a leg.

idioms.en: to boast or gloat about something
idioms.mnemonic: A cock crows loudly as if boasting.
idioms.example: He kept crowing over his victory in the chess match.

idioms.en: a warning or appeal that nobody heeds
idioms.hi: अनसुनी पुकार; नक्कारखाने में तूती की आवाज़
idioms.mnemonic: A cry in an empty desert that no one hears.
idioms.example: His warnings about pollution were a cry in the wilderness.

idioms.en: to regret uselessly what cannot be undone
idioms.mnemonic: Spilt milk cannot go back into the glass.
idioms.example: You failed once; don't cry over spilt milk, prepare again.

idioms.en: to create a poor impression
idioms.hi: बुरा प्रभाव छोड़ना; हँसी का पात्र बनना
idioms.mnemonic: 'Figure' = appearance; a sorry (pitiable) appearance.
idioms.example: Without preparation, he cut a sorry figure at the interview.

idioms.en: to be very similar in nature or character
idioms.hi: एक जैसे स्वभाव का होना; एक ही मिट्टी के बने होना
idioms.mnemonic: Two pieces cut from one cloth look alike.
idioms.example: The two brothers are cut from the same cloth: both are generous.

idioms.en: one who argues against something just for the sake of argument
idioms.hi: केवल बहस के लिए विरोधी पक्ष रखने वाला
idioms.mnemonic: The Church once appointed a 'devil's advocate' to argue against making someone a saint.
idioms.example: I agree with you, but let me play devil's advocate for a moment.

idioms.en: to render a service or help someone
idioms.mnemonic: A 'turn' here means a deed; a good deed.
idioms.example: Scouts are taught to do a good turn every day.

idioms.word: don't judge a book by its cover
idioms.en: do not judge someone or something by outward appearance
idioms.hi: सूरत से सीरत का अंदाज़ा मत लगाओ
idioms.mnemonic: A dull cover may hide a great story.
idioms.example: Shyama looks innocent but is cunning; don't judge a book by its cover.

idioms.word: don't put all your eggs in one basket
idioms.en: don't risk everything on a single venture
idioms.hi: सारा जोखिम एक ही जगह मत लगाओ
idioms.mnemonic: Drop one basket and you lose all the eggs.
idioms.example: Invest in different schemes; don't put all your eggs in one basket.

idioms.en: to retract what one has said; admit one was wrong
idioms.mnemonic: Swallowing the very words you spoke.
idioms.example: He said I would fail, but my result made him eat his words.

idioms.en: enough space or freedom to act as one wishes
idioms.hi: काम करने की आज़ादी; पर्याप्त जगह
idioms.mnemonic: Room to move your elbows freely.
idioms.example: Good managers give their teams enough elbow room.

idioms.en: something done only for show; a deception
idioms.mnemonic: Washing someone's eyes so they see a false picture.
idioms.example: The inquiry was a mere eyewash to calm the public.

idioms.en: to accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions
idioms.mnemonic: An offender drummed out of an army regiment faced the band's music.
idioms.example: You broke the rule, so now you must face the music.

idioms.en: a friend who is unreliable in times of difficulty
idioms.mnemonic: Stays with you only when the weather (time) is fair.
idioms.example: He proved to be a fair-weather friend when I lost my job.

idioms.en: over a large area; in all directions
idioms.mnemonic: Far in distance, wide in spread.
idioms.example: People came from far and wide to see the fair.

idioms.en: an unwanted or unnecessary person
idioms.mnemonic: A car needs only four wheels.
idioms.example: At their anniversary dinner I felt like a fifth wheel.

idioms.en: to avoid something
idioms.mnemonic: A shy person keeps away.
idioms.example: He always fights shy of taking responsibility.

idioms.en: to fight very fiercely
idioms.mnemonic: Fighting with teeth and nails, like an animal.
idioms.example: The villagers fought tooth and nail to save their land.

idioms.en: strong determination and ambition
idioms.mnemonic: A fire burning inside drives you forward.
idioms.example: All the candidates have fire in their bellies to succeed.

idioms.en: most importantly; before anything else
idioms.mnemonic: First + foremost (front-most): doubly first.
idioms.example: First and foremost, we must ensure everyone's safety.

idioms.en: a person who feels uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings
idioms.hi: असहज महसूस करना; बेगानी जगह में बेचैन
idioms.mnemonic: A fish cannot be at ease on land.
idioms.example: The village boy felt like a fish out of water in the big city.

idioms.en: to lose one's temper suddenly
idioms.mnemonic: A loose axe-head flies off its handle without warning.
idioms.example: He flies off the handle at the smallest mistake.

idioms.en: a short nap
idioms.mnemonic: A wink = a brief closing of the eyes.
idioms.example: Grandfather takes forty winks after lunch.

idioms.en: lively and energetic
idioms.mnemonic: Horses fed on beans were full of energy.
idioms.example: The children were full of beans on the first day of the holidays.

idioms.en: talking nonsense; boastful empty talk
idioms.hi: बकवास करने वाला; खोखली बातें करने वाला
idioms.mnemonic: Hot air is light and empty.
idioms.example: Don't believe his promises; he is full of hot air.

idioms.en: to become nervous and lose courage before doing something
idioms.mnemonic: Fear makes your feet cold and unwilling to move.
idioms.example: He got cold feet just before the speech.

idioms.en: to annoy or irritate someone
idioms.mnemonic: Like something stuck in your hair, bothering you.
idioms.example: The noisy kids were getting in everyone's hair.

idioms.en: to irritate or annoy someone
idioms.mnemonic: Taking away someone's pet goat makes them angry.
idioms.example: His constant interruptions really get my goat.

idioms.en: the ability to speak fluently and persuasively
idioms.mnemonic: 'Gab' means talk.
idioms.example: With her gift of the gab, she can sell anything.

idioms.en: mutual adjustment and cooperation
idioms.mnemonic: Both sides give and both sides take.
idioms.example: A happy family runs on give and take.

idioms.en: to submit something
idioms.mnemonic: Put it into the teacher's hand.
idioms.example: Please hand in your assignments by Friday.

idioms.en: a difficult problem or person to deal with
idioms.mnemonic: A hard shell resists cracking.
idioms.example: The new manager is a hard nut to crack.

idioms.en: to have a selfish motive
idioms.hi: स्वार्थ होना; अपना उल्लू सीधा करना
idioms.mnemonic: Story: a man flattered a boy into grinding his axe for him.
idioms.example: He has no axe to grind; his advice is honest.

idioms.en: to be very busy
idioms.mnemonic: No free hand left to take anything else.
idioms.example: I can't take a new project; I have my hands full.

idioms.word: have one's heart in one's mouth
idioms.en: to be extremely frightened or anxious
idioms.hi: डर के मारे कलेजा मुँह को आना
idioms.mnemonic: Fear makes the heart seem to jump up to the mouth.
idioms.example: I had my heart in my mouth as the car skidded.

idioms.en: to attack or behave unfairly
idioms.mnemonic: In boxing, hitting below the belt is against the rules.
idioms.example: Mocking his illness in the debate was hitting below the belt.

idioms.en: to go to bed
idioms.mnemonic: Sack = a mattress once stuffed in a sack.
idioms.example: I was so tired that I hit the sack at nine.

idioms.en: to keep or retain something
idioms.mnemonic: Holding something tightly so it doesn't slip.
idioms.example: Hold onto that thought; it will be a great idea someday.

idioms.en: wait; be patient; slow down
idioms.mnemonic: Riders hold the reins to stop horses rushing.
idioms.example: Hold your horses! Let's read the instructions first.

idioms.en: a loud public outcry or protest
idioms.mnemonic: Old English law: a 'hue and cry' was raised to chase a criminal.
idioms.example: There was a great hue and cry over the fare hike.

idioms.word: if you play with fire, you'll get burned
idioms.en: if you do something dangerous, you will suffer harm
idioms.mnemonic: Fire burns whoever plays with it.
idioms.example: He teased the dog till it bit him; if you play with fire, you'll get burned.

idioms.en: at the height of activity
idioms.mnemonic: A swing moving at its highest arc.
idioms.example: Wedding preparations are in full swing.

idioms.en: in trouble
idioms.mnemonic: Being dipped in hot water is painful.
idioms.example: He landed in hot water for breaking the vase.

idioms.en: because of; considering
idioms.mnemonic: Seeing a matter in the light of facts.
idioms.example: In light of the heavy rain, the match was postponed.

idioms.en: all the details of something
idioms.mnemonic: Knowing every way in and every way out.
idioms.example: She knows the ins and outs of tax law.

idioms.en: to stay cheerful and positive in difficulty
idioms.mnemonic: A lowered chin shows defeat; keep it raised.
idioms.example: Keep your chin up; you'll do better next time.

idioms.en: to remain calm in a difficult situation
idioms.mnemonic: Don't 'lose your head'; keep it.
idioms.example: She kept her head during the fire and led everyone out.

idioms.en: to keep someone informed of the latest news
idioms.mnemonic: Like regular letters by post.
idioms.example: Please keep me posted about the project's progress.

idioms.en: to consult and think together
idioms.mnemonic: Heads close together, sharing ideas.
idioms.example: If we lay our heads together, we'll find a solution.

idioms.en: to listen attentively
idioms.mnemonic: Give your ear to someone for a while.
idioms.example: A good friend always lends an ear to your problems.

idioms.en: support expressed in words but not in action
idioms.mnemonic: Service only from the lips, not the heart.
idioms.example: Many leaders pay only lip service to women's safety.

idioms.en: to rely on someone or something for help
idioms.mnemonic: Looking towards someone for support.
idioms.example: Farmers look to the monsoon for a good harvest.

idioms.en: to go mad; lose one's mind
idioms.mnemonic: Marbles once meant one's wits or senses.
idioms.example: He must have lost his marbles to quit such a good job.

idioms.en: to make up for a wrong one has done
idioms.mnemonic: Amend = to correct.
idioms.example: He apologised and tried to make amends for his rudeness.

idioms.en: to understand something (usually used in the negative)
idioms.hi: कुछ समझ पाना (प्रायः 'कुछ समझ न आना')
idioms.mnemonic: Can't tell the head from the tail of a coin.
idioms.example: I couldn't make head or tail of his handwriting.

idioms.en: a confused, complicated situation; also a false discovery
idioms.mnemonic: Horses don't build nests; it's an illusion and a mess.
idioms.example: The tangled wires behind the TV were a mare's nest.

idioms.en: to suffer a final, decisive defeat
idioms.mnemonic: Napoleon was finally defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
idioms.example: The champion met his Waterloo in the final round.

idioms.en: to lose an opportunity
idioms.mnemonic: Arriving after the boat has sailed.
idioms.example: Apply today or you will miss the boat.

idioms.en: something that attracts attention for a short time only
idioms.mnemonic: Old saying: a wonder lasts nine days and then fades.
idioms.example: The viral video was just a nine days' wonder.

idioms.en: to speak frankly and directly
idioms.mnemonic: Mince = cut into small pieces; he doesn't soften his words.
idioms.example: The coach did not mince words about the team's poor play.

idioms.en: not something one likes or is interested in
idioms.mnemonic: Tea lovers are fussy about their own cup.
idioms.example: Thank you, but clubbing is not my cup of tea.

idioms.en: extremely happy
idioms.mnemonic: Cloud nine was the highest cloud in old weather classification.
idioms.example: She was on cloud nine after topping the exam.

idioms.en: in a state of anxious suspense
idioms.mnemonic: Cloth was stretched tight on hooks called tenterhooks.
idioms.example: We were on tenterhooks waiting for the results.

idioms.en: very quickly; at once
idioms.mnemonic: Army command to march at double speed.
idioms.example: The sergeant told the soldiers to report on the double.

idioms.word: on the spur of the moment
idioms.en: suddenly, without planning; impulsively
idioms.mnemonic: A spur suddenly makes a horse jump forward.
idioms.example: On the spur of the moment, we decided to go to Goa.

idioms.en: declining; decreasing
idioms.mnemonic: The moon wanes as it grows smaller.
idioms.example: Interest in the old game is on the wane.

idioms.en: a mind that thinks about only one thing
idioms.hi: एक ही बात पर अटका दिमाग़
idioms.mnemonic: A train on one track cannot turn anywhere else.
idioms.example: He has a one-track mind; he only thinks about cricket.

idioms.en: beyond one's ability to understand
idioms.mnemonic: The idea flew above your head, not into it.
idioms.example: The lecture on quantum physics went over my head.

idioms.en: a very annoying person or thing
idioms.mnemonic: A stiff neck is constantly irritating.
idioms.example: Filling forms manually every year is a pain in the neck.

idioms.en: something very easy to do
idioms.mnemonic: As easy as eating a slice of cake.
idioms.example: The first question was a piece of cake.

idioms.en: to make every possible effort
idioms.mnemonic: Pulling all the stops on a church organ gives full volume.
idioms.example: The team pulled out all the stops for the presentation.

idioms.en: to tease or joke with someone
idioms.mnemonic: Playfully tripping someone up.
idioms.example: Don't worry, I was just pulling your leg.

idioms.en: to extinguish a fire or light
idioms.mnemonic: Put the flame 'out' of existence.
idioms.example: The firefighters quickly put out the fire.

idioms.en: to understand the hidden or implied meaning
idioms.mnemonic: The real message hides in the space between the lines.
idioms.example: Reading between the lines, I knew she was unhappy.

idioms.en: to emerge with new life after destruction or failure
idioms.hi: राख से फिर उठ खड़ा होना; नवजीवन पाना
idioms.mnemonic: The mythical phoenix is reborn from its own ashes.
idioms.example: The city rose like a phoenix after the earthquake.

idioms.en: to disturb a stable situation
idioms.mnemonic: Rocking a boat risks tipping everyone out.
idioms.example: Things are going well, so don't rock the boat.

idioms.en: an overly positive or optimistic view
idioms.hi: हर चीज़ को अच्छा ही देखना; आशावादी दृष्टि
idioms.mnemonic: Pink lenses make everything look pleasant.
idioms.example: She sees the world through rose-coloured glasses.

idioms.en: to be very busy without achieving much
idioms.mnemonic: Running in a circle brings you back to the start.
idioms.example: Without a plan, the team kept running around in circles.

idioms.en: to face difficulties
idioms.mnemonic: A ship sailing into a storm.
idioms.example: Their partnership ran into rough weather last year.

idioms.en: to avoid taking sides
idioms.mnemonic: Sitting on a fence, you are on neither side.
idioms.example: Many people are still sitting on the fence over the issue.

idioms.en: a secret or early preview of something
idioms.mnemonic: Sneak = secretly; peek = quick look.
idioms.example: The company gave us a sneak peek of its new phone.

idioms.en: to reveal a secret
idioms.mnemonic: Ancient voting with beans: spilling the jar revealed the result.
idioms.example: Who spilled the beans about the surprise party?

idioms.en: to laugh uncontrollably
idioms.mnemonic: Laughing so hard your sides could burst.
idioms.example: The comedian's jokes made us split our sides.

idioms.en: to spread very quickly
idioms.mnemonic: A forest fire spreads unstoppably.
idioms.example: The news of his victory spread like wildfire.

idioms.en: a fair and honest deal
idioms.mnemonic: Square = fair and straight.
idioms.example: The workers only want a square deal from the company.

idioms.en: a very short distance
idioms.hi: थोड़ी सी दूरी पर; पास में
idioms.mnemonic: As far as you can throw a stone.
idioms.example: The station is just a stone's throw from my house.

idioms.word: strain at a gnat and swallow a camel
idioms.en: to fuss over small matters while ignoring big ones
idioms.hi: छोटी बातों पर ध्यान देना, बड़ी को अनदेखा करना
idioms.mnemonic: From the Bible: straining out a tiny insect but gulping a camel.
idioms.example: Fining a clerk for being late while ignoring the big scam is straining at a gnat and swallowing a camel.

idioms.en: to deal with dangerous or ruthless people
idioms.hi: खतरनाक लोगों के बीच काम करना
idioms.mnemonic: Sharks are dangerous predators.
idioms.example: In the stock market, you often swim with sharks.

idioms.en: to object to; be offended by
idioms.mnemonic: 'Exception' here means objection: you raise an objection to it.
idioms.example: She took exception to his rude remarks.

idioms.en: to make great efforts
idioms.mnemonic: Taking on pain (effort) to do something well.
idioms.example: He took pains to make the project perfect.

idioms.en: to assess or review a situation
idioms.mnemonic: Shopkeepers count their stock to know their position.
idioms.example: Let us take stock of the situation before acting.

idioms.word: take with a pinch of salt
idioms.en: to doubt the truth of something
idioms.hi: किसी बात पर पूरा विश्वास न करना
idioms.mnemonic: A little salt made doubtful food easier to swallow.
idioms.example: Take his stories with a pinch of salt.

idioms.en: boastful or exaggerated talk
idioms.mnemonic: Words that are 'taller' than reality.
idioms.example: His claims of meeting the President are just tall talk.

idioms.en: there is nothing more to be said; it's finished
idioms.mnemonic: A letter that ends with nothing more written.
idioms.example: We lost the final match, and that's all she wrote.

idioms.en: to deliberately ignore something
idioms.mnemonic: Nelson put the telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal.
idioms.example: The guard turned a blind eye to the late arrivals.

idioms.en: to pass the critical stage and begin to improve
idioms.mnemonic: Turning the corner of a road leaves the bad stretch behind.
idioms.example: The patient has finally turned the corner.

idioms.word: two heads are better than one
idioms.en: two people working together solve problems better than one
idioms.hi: दो दिमाग़ एक से बेहतर; मिलकर काम आसान
idioms.mnemonic: Twice the thinking power.
idioms.example: Let's solve this together; two heads are better than one.

idioms.en: of the required standard
idioms.mnemonic: Reaching the line (mark) set as the standard.
idioms.example: His performance was not up to the mark.

idioms.en: past events that are no longer important
idioms.hi: बीती ताहि बिसार दे; बीती बात
idioms.mnemonic: Water that has flowed away never returns.
idioms.example: Our old quarrel is water under the bridge now.

idioms.word: wear one's heart on one's sleeve
idioms.en: to show one's feelings openly
idioms.mnemonic: Knights wore their lady's colours on their sleeves.
idioms.example: She wears her heart on her sleeve, so we know when she's upset.
